title: Debt and Cipher
premise: Felix Reyes, a burned-out private security contractor, discovers the safe house she was supposed to be guarding has been listed for sale online — with interior photos revealing classified documents and the face of a witness who was declared dead. The listing is bait: someone inside her own firm is selling protected identities to three governments circling a fragile summit. As Felix traces the leak from Vienna to a coastal villa, she realizes the 'dead' witness is alive, hiding in plain sight as the assassin hired to erase her. In the end, Felix chooses truth over loyalty to her employer, exposing the broker at the summit itself — and walks away with no client, no firm, and, for the first time since the incident, a full night's sleep ahead of her.
about_author: Odile Voss is a former risk analyst who spent a decade writing threat assessments for people whose names never appeared in print. She now writes thrillers from a rented farmhouse in Portugal, where the only thing under surveillance is her olive grove.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Insomniac and hollowed out by an earlier failure, Felix scrolls property listings at 3 a.m. and finds the safe house — her safe house — photographed room by room, including the locked study that should not exist on any camera. When she reports it, her firm stonewalls her within the hour. The emotional beat is dread sharpening into suspicion: the enemy isn't outside the walls; it signed her paychecks.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Felix and a weary intelligence liaison named Amara Okafor. Following the listing's metadata, Felix learns buyers from three governments are bidding on access to the summit's security detail, while Amara realizes her own agency may be a customer. They collide uneasily in Vienna, trading half-truths. The beat is wary alliance: two women who trust nothing discovering they need each other's pieces of the puzzle.

chapters.title: The Buyer Who Blinks
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, closing on the assassin's. Tracing the escrow payments to a coastal villa, Felix corners the broker — and finds the 'dead' witness alive, working as the very assassin contracted to finish the job. The assassin offers Felix a choice: take the payout and disappear, or burn everything including herself. Climactic beat: loyalty vs. truth made flesh, with Felix choosing truth at gunpoint and barely escaping with proof.

chapters.title: Open Session
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, converging on Felix. At the summit, Felix goes off-book, delivering the evidence past security, past her ex-employer's lawyers, and past the assassin sent to stop her — whom she talks down rather than kills. The broker is exposed; the witness surfaces alive; Amara burns her own agency's file to protect them both. Resolution beat: belonging found not in a firm or flag, but in the choice to tell the truth together.
